draft.title: Managing population growth in Sydney
card: Sydney's population is growing, so the city needs more homes, jobs and services. Planners use several ways to manage this growth.
Large new suburbs are built on the edge of the city, especially in the west. They add many homes but need new roads, schools and services.
More homes, such as apartments, are built near train lines in existing suburbs. Residents can then reach work and services by public transport.
New transport, such as the Sydney Metro, helps people cross the city. Residents may worry about traffic or lost local character, councils about services, and developers about cost.
draft.remember: Sydney manages growth with new western suburbs, more homes near trains and new transport, and groups can disagree about it.

a.q: Which strategy puts more homes near existing train lines in Sydney?
opts: New suburbs on the western edge
a.why: Building more homes, such as apartments, near train lines is higher density housing. New suburbs are built on the edge of the city, and a Metro line is transport, not housing.
a.clue: Think about where the homes are built, not about the trains.

b.q: A developer plans apartments beside a train station in an established Sydney suburb. Some nearby residents object. What is the most likely reason?
opts: They worry about more traffic and local character
They want the new homes built on farmland in the west
They think the station will be closed after the building
They believe the apartments will lower the city's population
b.why: Residents may worry about traffic and a change in local character when density rises. The other options do not fit: the plan is near a train station, and apartments add homes for a growing population rather than lowering it.
b.clue: Residents who already live there see their street change.

b.best: They worry about more traffic and local character
